chain.title: A Workshop Begins
chain.desc: Andesite Alloy is the starting material for your mechanical workshop. Set some aside for shafts and casings; those lead to power transmission and your first processing machines.

chain.title: Carry the Motion
chain.desc: Connect shafts to a rotating power source to carry rotation in a straight line. Start with a short, accessible drive shaft so you can attach new machines as the workshop grows.

chain.title: Around the Corner
chain.desc: Cogwheels transfer rotation between adjacent mechanisms. Combine small and large cogs when you need to change speed, and check the direction before joining two powered lines.

chain.title: The River Pays Rent
chain.desc: Place the Water Wheel where flowing water can turn it, then connect its axle to your drive shaft. This gives the workshop a renewable starting source of rotation.

chain.title: A Frame for the Workshop
chain.desc: Andesite Casing is used by many early machines. Prepare a small supply before branching into pressing, milling and mechanical tools.

chain.title: A Place to Work
chain.desc: A Depot holds an item at a fixed workstation. Put one below your press for a simple first processing setup before you invest in moving items on belts.

chain.title: The Hammer Falls
chain.desc: Connect rotation to the Mechanical Press and place a Depot or belt below its head. Process an ingot into a sheet, then collect the result. Sheets open a new set of components and tools.

chain.title: Your First Sheet
chain.desc: Use the press to turn iron into sheets. Keep the press connected: sheets are useful components throughout the workshop, so this is a workstation worth leaving assembled.

chain.title: A More Precise Workshop
chain.desc: Press gold into sheets for the next group of tools and mechanisms. Add a place to collect the output so small components do not get lost around the press.

chain.title: The Engineer's Thumb
chain.desc: Use the Wrench to adjust the orientation of Create blocks and dismantle supported machinery. Keep it with you whenever you expand or rearrange the workshop.

chain.title: Read Your Machines
chain.desc: Wear the Engineer's Goggles while inspecting your machinery. Their readouts make it much easier to understand speed, stress and why an overloaded network has stopped.

chain.title: Stone That Chews
chain.desc: Power a Millstone and feed it a supported processing input. Check the available milling recipes, then collect the output before deciding which resource to automate next.

chain.title: Keep Things Moving
chain.desc: Use the Belt Connector on two suitable shafts to create a Mechanical Belt. Give the belt rotation and watch which direction it carries items before adding input and output containers.

chain.title: Feed the Line
chain.desc: Use Andesite Funnels to move items between containers and your processing line. Connect an input chest and an output chest so the first machine can run without constant hand feeding.

chain.title: Boring Through
chain.desc: Power the Mechanical Drill to break blocks in front of it, or incorporate it into a moving contraption. Plan somewhere for the mined items to go before you scale up.

chain.title: A Timber Workshop
chain.desc: Use the Mechanical Saw for supported cutting recipes and tree cutting. Connect item collection alongside the saw so the wood becomes a usable supply instead of a pile on the ground.

chain.title: Processing on the Breeze
chain.desc: An Encased Fan moves air when powered. Passing that airflow through the appropriate processing medium lets you wash, smoke or blast supported items. Check the recipe and keep the items in the airflow until processing finishes.

chain.title: Room to Mix
chain.desc: Place a Basin below a Mechanical Mixer or Mechanical Press for supported batch recipes. Leave space underneath if the recipe needs a heat source.

chain.title: Bring Back a Flame
chain.desc: Take an Empty Blaze Burner to a blaze and capture it. The resulting burner is the heat source for recipes that need a heated Basin.

chain.title: A Captive Flame
chain.desc: Place the Blaze Burner below your Basin and provide the fuel required by the recipe. Heated and superheated recipes are different requirements, so check the recipe before feeding the machine.

chain.title: Stirring the Pot
chain.desc: Suspend the Mechanical Mixer above a Basin and connect sufficient rotational speed. Add a complete supported recipe to the Basin; provide heat underneath when the recipe calls for it.

chain.title: The Second Metal
chain.desc: Build a supply of Zinc Ingots for brass production. Follow the processing recipes available in this pack to turn the raw resource into metal.

chain.title: Copper Meets Zinc
chain.desc: Prepare a heated mixing setup for brass. This material leads to more precise item handling and a new family of machines, so leave the setup ready for later batches.

chain.title: A Smarter Factory
chain.desc: Brass Casing supports the workshop’s more advanced machinery. Use it to expand into controlled routing and automatic crafting.

chain.title: Polish the Signal
chain.desc: Polish Rose Quartz using Sand Paper. The polished component leads to Electron Tubes, which are used in several advanced Create devices.

chain.title: A Little Intelligence
chain.desc: Make Electron Tubes for advanced machinery such as Mechanical Crafters and Deployers. Prepare the components before expanding a whole bank of machines.

chain.title: The Factory Builds for You
chain.desc: Arrange Mechanical Crafters in the shape required by a supported recipe. Point their transfer arrows toward the final output, provide rotation and feed each position its ingredient.

chain.title: A Mechanical Hand
chain.desc: A Deployer performs supported item-use actions for you. Give it the appropriate held item and use it as a workstation in sequenced assembly.

chain.title: A Sequence, Not a Single Craft
chain.desc: Follow the Precision Mechanism’s sequenced assembly recipe in order. Keep the unfinished component moving through the required steps until the full sequence finishes, then collect the result.

chain.title: The Workshop Goes Places
chain.desc: Prepare Train Casing for railway equipment. Before building the train, choose a route and leave room for a station and an assembly track.

chain.title: Lay the Route
chain.desc: Lay a short, usable stretch of Train Track. Begin with enough straight track to assemble a carriage, then extend it into the route you want to serve.

chain.title: All Aboard
chain.desc: Place a Train Station beside the track and use its assembly controls to build a train. Name the stop clearly so it is easy to recognize when you later create a schedule.

notes: Verified against create-1.20.1-6.0.8.jar. Every chain and collection id is present as assets/create/models/item/<id>.json, except create:encased_fluid_pipe which is lang-only (block.create.encased_fluid_pipe) and is kept under the block-lang rule. Recipe sources read: data/create/recipes/crafting/{materials,kinetics,logistics,appliances}/*, item_application/* for all four casings (andesite/brass/copper/railway casings are right-click applications onto stripped logs or wood, NOT grid recipes), mixing/brass_ingot.json (copper + zinc in a heated basin - this is why blaze_burner and mechanical_mixer sit ahead of brass in the chain), sandpaper_polishing/rose_quartz.json, sequenced_assembly/precision_mechanism.json (gold sheet plus five deployer loops), and sequenced_assembly/track.json. Ponder: assets/create/ponder/ ships only bare .nbt scene layouts with no order index (scene registration lives in code), so no ponder-derived ordering was used; the sole ordering hint in assets is the single chapter texture 'basic_kinetics', which is consistent with shaft/cogwheel/water wheel being the first tier. PACK CONSENSUS vs RECIPES: moddb puts create:copper_diving_helmet at pos 0.092 and create:copper_backtank at pos 0.204 (19 packs each), i.e. the diving set as an early-game reward roughly level with andesite_casing (0.202, 36 packs), even though the backtank costs a full copper block plus andesite alloy and a shaft. Consensus was preferred over the recipe reading: the diving set is NOT pushed to the endgame, it is broken out as its own collection wheel so packs can gate it early. moddb also ranks create:shaft (0.098, 43 packs) and create:andesite_alloy (0.059, 39 packs) as the two most common Create quests overall, matching the chain head exactly. Consensus items left out of the 24-step spine because they are cosmetic or side branches (all verified present in the jar, safe as optional quests): white_table_cloth, red_table_cloth, red_sand_paper, andesite_door, brown_toolbox, item_hatch, white_postbox, builders_tea, crafting_blueprint, purple_seat, scorchia, sail_frame, bound_cardboard_block, cardboard_helmet, cardboard_sword, crushed_raw_iron, crushed_raw_gold. DROPPED: create:deforester - not in this jar (it is a Create: Above and Beyond item); no other candidate failed verification.
